subject: Remittance split causing AR double-apply & proposed JV correction
messages:
From: Marta Alvarez <marta.alvarez@halcyoncloud.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Payment application mismatch — remittance split (INV-4451 / INV-4470)

Hi Rohan,

We processed the wire for Halcyon Cloud on 2026-06-10 (see attached remittance PDF) and the payment shows up split across two invoices on our side (INV-4451 and INV-4470). When we matched against Redwood's AR, it appears one portion was applied to INV-4451 and the other portion was posted as a credit (unapplied) to a suspense account, which is now causing duplicate outstanding amounts on both the customer and GL.

Quick details: 
- Total payment: $28,450.00 (incl. VAT)
- Wire notes reference: HC-20260610-WIRE
- Halcyon expected allocation: $18,200 -> INV-4451, $10,250 -> INV-4470

Could your team trace how the second piece ended up in suspense? We need the correct AR allocation and, if required, a prior-period journal correction so revenue recognition and AR-aging reflect the true state for June close. Attaching our AP register export (ap_register_q2.csv) and the remittance stub.

Thanks,
Marta Alvarez
Finance Operations Manager
Halcyon Cloud

Attachments: remittance_20260610.pdf (pdf), ap_register_q2.csv (csv)

From: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>
To: Marta Alvarez <marta.alvarez@halcyoncloud.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Payment application mismatch — remittance split (INV-4451 / INV-4470)

Hi Marta — thanks for the detail and attachments.

I've pulled the AR ledger lines and can see the same split. We're looping finance (Laura) and revenue ops (Grace) to confirm whether an auto-apply rule misinterpreted the remittance notes and pushed the smaller amount to Suspense GL 1199. Laura — can you confirm whether the unapplied credit can be re-applied manually to INV-4470 or if we should run a JV to clear the suspense and correct revenue mapping?

For auditing, please confirm whether Halcyon wants the original invoices reissued or if a JV + memo to the customer is acceptable. We're prepared to do a prior-period adjustment if necessary (June close).

I'll keep you posted with ledger IDs.

Best,
Rohan Mehta
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rohan.mehta@redwood.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>, Marta Alvarez <marta.alvarez@halcyoncloud.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 13:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Payment application mismatch — remittance split (INV-4451 / INV-4470)

Thanks for flagging, Marta and Rohan. I reviewed the ledger and our AR-autoapply logs: the payment was ingested as two lines because the remittance parser saw two reference strings and created two allocation candidates; the second candidate failed validation against open invoices and fell back to Suspense GL 1199.

Proposed remediation (recommended):
1) Create a reversing JV dated 2026-06-30 to move the $10,250 from Suspense GL 1199 back to Cash (clear the credit).
2) Post a manual application entry to apply $10,250 to INV-4470 (AR subledger update).
3) Run a revenue reclassification entry if the initial recognition used the incorrect RevMap (I flagged INV-4470 as mapped to RevCode 3200 instead of 3100 in the revmap_proposal.xlsx).
4) Produce a memo for Halcyon describing the correction and the effect on AR aging and revenue (prior-period adjustment; immaterial to P&L but affects AR days).

I'll attach the proposed JV and the revmap spreadsheet for your review. If Halcyon prefers invoice reissue instead of a JV, that adds a re-billing flow and potential collection friction — my recommendation is JV + memo to keep customer experience smooth.

Next steps:
- Marta: confirm acceptance of JV + memo (or request reissue).
- Rohan: please confirm cutover date for June close so we time the JV entry.
- Grace: loop in Revenue Ops to confirm RevCode reclass doesn't trigger a retrospective revenue recognition change in our GL subsystem.

Laura Bennett
Accounting Manager, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

Attachments: revmap_proposal.xlsx (xlsx)

Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2026 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Payment application mismatch — remittance split (INV-4451 / INV-4470)

Thanks, Laura — JV + memo is fine with us. We prefer to avoid invoice reissuance. Please proceed with the reversing JV dated 2026-06-30 and the manual application to INV-4470.

A couple of asks for audit completeness: 
- Could you include the original remittance PDF and the AP register extract as supporting attachments in the memo?
- Please confirm the GL entry IDs when posted so we can reconcile on our side.

Once posted, we'll mark both invoices as fully paid on Halcyon records. Appreciate the fast turnaround — June close is tight for us as well.

Best regards,
Marta Alvarez
Finance Operations Manager
Halcyon Cloud
